text:
Alex: hey all, new hire here. trying to pull our private docker image from home on Windows 11 WSL2 and it fails with connection reset. company WireGuard client shows I'm assigned 10.4.9.15 and allowed-ips include 10.4.0.0/16, but `docker pull registry.internal.redwood:5000/repo/image:latest` just errors out. anyone seen WSL2 + split-tunnel weirdness?
Mira: welcome Alex! i've hit this before. can you paste the docker error and `ip route` from inside WSL?
Alex: error from Docker Desktop UI and CLI: `Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry.internal.redwood:5000/v2/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout`
Alex: WSL `ip route`:
```
default via 172.21.240.1 dev eth0
172.21.240.0/20 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 172.21.240.2
```
Alex: Windows `wg show` (client):
```
interface: wg-win
  peer: PPLLLLL
    allowed ips: 10.4.0.0/16, 172.19.0.0/16
    endpoint: vpn.redwood.company:51820
assigned ip: 10.4.9.15
```
eng-sre-bot: Note: your account policy: split-tunnel. registry.internal.redwood is 10.4.20.14 (internal only).
IT-ops: WSL2 uses a NAT network and doesn't inherit Windows routing for some multi-homed setups. so your WSL default route goes via the WSL virtual NIC and Windows host isn't forwarding traffic for 10.4/16 unless explicitly configured.
DevOps: quick repro: inside WSL try `curl -v --interface 172.21.240.2 http://10.4.20.14:5000/v2/` (HTTP) and `curl -v --interface 172.21.240.2 https://10.4.20.14:5000/v2/` (HTTPS). that helps pinpoint tunnel vs routing.
Alex: `curl` to 10.4.20.14 from WSL timed out. from Windows powershell `curl http://10.4.20.14:5000` works.
Mira: yup that means Windows host can reach internal registry via WireGuard but WSL traffic isn't being NATed/forwarded correctly. two options: (1) add a static route on Windows that forces the registry through the wg interface and enable forwarding to WSL, (2) use an SSH/docker context proxy via bastion while we patch configs.
IT-ops: workaround we push to new hires: create a docker context that uses the bastion SSH tunnel so you can pull without adjusting host networking. commands:
```
docker context create redwood --docker "host=ssh://bastionsvc@bastion.redwood"
docker --context redwood pull registry.internal.redwood:5000/repo/image:latest
```
IT-ops: it uses the bastion account (we auto-authorize dev images for new hires). this is quick while we roll a proper client-side fix.
Alex: tried the docker context trick. `docker --context redwood pull` started the transfer and finished. nice!
DevOps: long-term fix options: enable ip_forward on Windows and add NAT rule so WSL packets to 10.4.0.0/16 use the WireGuard interface. on Win11 you can run `netsh interface ipv4 add route 10.4.0.0/16 "WireGuard" <metric>` or set the WG client to use a WSL-friendly adapter mode.
Mira: we also have a label we add to onboarding profiles: `wg-wsl-forward` (ticket ONB-5012). DM IT-ops with your new hire ticket and we'll add it so your Windows host is configured during provisioning.
Alex: can you confirm what I should ask support for in the ticket?
IT-ops: say: "Please enable wg-wsl-forward for <your-username> (ONB-5012)." we'll re-provision your WireGuard profile with the host-side forwarding rules.
eng-sre-bot: Tip: if you often work from home, consider using the bastion docker context for heavy image pulls to avoid transient MTU/NAT issues.
Alex: thanks everyone, pulling images works now via the bastion. appreciate the speedy help and the warm welcome :wave:
